traits.culm_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Carex obnupta: culms 50 cm to 1.5 m tall.

appearance.organs.panicle.note: The inflorescence, the model's choice after FNA's account of the species (volume 23, Standley, Cayouette and Bruederle), as search results quote it (the page was not read): arching spikes, at least the lowest hanging, 2 or 3 male and 2 to 5 female, the lowest female spike 2.5 to 15 cm long and 5 to 10 mm wide; its scales red-brown, longer and wider than the perigynia, which are 2.2 to 3.8 mm. Drawn as 6 long spikes on short stalks spaced up the axis, which arches over 30 degrees by its tip, each spike with the spikelet card (a sedge spike is a spike of one-flowered spikelets): 40 scales in a spiral. Colours by eye: dark red-brown.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a tall, coarse sedge forming dense colonies of stiff, dark, glossy, keeled leaves with dark brown flower spikes on three-angled stems. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1.2 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dark glossy green leaves; dark brown spikes.
